subproblem.title: Slice bound on a convex set: ∫⁻_Q∫⁻_Q g((1 − t)y + tx) ≤ 2ⁿ Lⁿ(Q) ∫⁻_Q g
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, ℝⁿ := Euclid n with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ (volume), Q ⊆ ℝⁿ convex and measurable, g : ℝⁿ → [0, ∞] measurable, and t ∈ [0, 1]. Then ∫⁻_{x∈Q} ∫⁻_{y∈Q} g((1 − t)y + tx) dy dx ≤ 2ⁿ · Lⁿ(Q) · ∫⁻_Q g. All integrals are lower Lebesgue integrals in [0, ∞] (outer variable x, inner variable y), and the right side is computed in [0, ∞] with 0 · ∞ = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (Q : Set (Euclid n)) (g : Euclid n → ℝ≥0∞), Convex ℝ Q → MeasurableSet Q → Measurable g → ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∫⁻ x in Q, ∫⁻ y in Q, g ((1 - t) • y + t • x) ≤ 2 ^ n * volume Q * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–4 of the parent proof.
- For t ∈ [1/2, 1], change variables in one variable; the Jacobian is tⁿ.
- For t ∈ [0, 1/2), swap the order of integration and change variables in the other variable; the Jacobian is (1 − t)ⁿ.
- In both cases the image lies in Q by convexity, and the reciprocal of the Jacobian factor is at most 2ⁿ.

Here this is stated for an arbitrary convex measurable Q and a measurable g : ℝⁿ → [0, ∞], in lower-Lebesgue-integral form, so Tonelli needs no integrability hypothesis. The variables are named so that the inner variable y carries the weight 1 − t: the integrand is g((1 − t)y + tx). The same argument for Q = unit ball is the accepted Lean proof of Submission.dorag_ha_pb_slice_bound (commit 7ad779ea2).

Notation. ℝⁿ := Euclid n and Lⁿ := volume. ∫⁻ denotes lower Lebesgue integrals in [0, ∞], and products are taken in [0, ∞] with 0·∞ = 0. Fix t ∈ [0, 1].

1. One-variable bound. Claim: if c ∈ ℝⁿ, s ≥ 1/2, and c + s·v ∈ Q for every v ∈ Q, then ∫⁻_{v∈Q} g(c + s·v) dv ≤ 2ⁿ ∫⁻_Q g.
   Proof of the claim. Note s > 0. Let F := 1_Q·g, the extension of g|Q by 0; F is measurable because g and Q are.
   (a) For v ∈ Q we have c + s·v ∈ Q, so g(c + s·v) = F(c + s·v). Hence
       ∫⁻_{v∈Q} g(c + s·v) dv = ∫⁻_{v∈Q} F(c + s·v) dv ≤ ∫⁻_{ℝⁿ} F(c + s·v) dv.
   (b) The image of Lⁿ under the dilation v ↦ s·v is ofReal|s^{−n}|·Lⁿ = s^{−n}·Lⁿ (Measure.map_addHaar_smul, with finrank ℝ (Euclid n) = n, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). Therefore
       ∫⁻ F(c + s·v) dv = ∫⁻ F(c + w) d(map)(w) = s^{−n} ∫⁻ F(c + w) dw
       (lintegral_map, lintegral_smul_measure). By translation invariance of Lⁿ (lintegral_add_left_eq_self), this equals s^{−n} ∫⁻ F = s^{−n} ∫⁻_Q g (lintegral_indicator).
   (c) s ≥ 1/2 gives s^{−1} ≤ 2, hence ofReal(s^{−n}) = ofReal(s^{−1})ⁿ ≤ 2ⁿ.
   Combining (a)–(c) proves the claim.
2. Joint measurability. (x, y) ↦ g((1 − t)y + tx) is measurable on ℝⁿ × ℝⁿ: it is the measurable g composed with a continuous map.
3. Case t ≥ 1/2. By Tonelli for the s-finite measures Lⁿ restricted to Q (lintegral_lintegral_swap, using step 2),
   ∫⁻_{x∈Q} ∫⁻_{y∈Q} g((1 − t)y + tx) dy dx = ∫⁻_{y∈Q} ∫⁻_{x∈Q} g((1 − t)y + tx) dx dy.
   Fix y ∈ Q and apply step 1 with c := (1 − t)y and s := t ≥ 1/2. For x ∈ Q, c + t·x = (1 − t)y + tx lies in Q by convexity (weights 1 − t ≥ 0 and t ≥ 0 with sum 1). So the inner integral is ≤ 2ⁿ ∫⁻_Q g for every y ∈ Q. By monotonicity of the set integral over the measurable set Q (setLIntegral_mono') and setLIntegral_const, the whole expression is
   ≤ ∫⁻_{y∈Q} 2ⁿ ∫⁻_Q g = (2ⁿ ∫⁻_Q g)·Lⁿ(Q) = 2ⁿ·Lⁿ(Q)·∫⁻_Q g.
4. Case t ≤ 1/2. Fix x ∈ Q. Since (1 − t)y + tx = tx + (1 − t)y, apply step 1 with c := tx and s := 1 − t ≥ 1/2. For y ∈ Q, tx + (1 − t)y lies in Q by convexity. So ∫⁻_{y∈Q} g((1 − t)y + tx) dy ≤ 2ⁿ ∫⁻_Q g for every x ∈ Q. Integrating this constant bound over x ∈ Q exactly as in step 3 gives ≤ 2ⁿ·Lⁿ(Q)·∫⁻_Q g.
5. Every t ∈ [0, 1] satisfies t ≥ 1/2 or t ≤ 1/2, so steps 3–4 prove the statement. Finiteness of Lⁿ(Q) and of ∫⁻_Q g is never used: every step is an inequality in [0, ∞]. ∎

theorem Submission.cmcdt_cbm_sp_convex_slice_bound : ∀ (n : ℕ) (Q : Set (Euclid n)) (g : Euclid n → ℝ≥0∞), Convex ℝ Q → MeasurableSet Q → Measurable g → ∀ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∫⁻ x in Q, ∫⁻ y in Q, g ((1 - t) • y + t • x) ≤ 2 ^ n * volume Q * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z := by
  intro n Q g hQc hQm hg t ht
  obtain ⟨ht0, ht1⟩ := ht
  have key : ∀ (c : Euclid n) (s : ℝ), 1 / 2 ≤ s →
      (∀ v ∈ Q, c + s • v ∈ Q) →
      ∫⁻ v in Q, g (c + s • v) ≤ 2 ^ n * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z := by
    intro c s hs hcs
    have hs0 : 0 < s := by linarith
    obtain ⟨F, hFdef⟩ : ∃ F : Euclid n → ℝ≥0∞, F = Q.indicator g := ⟨_, rfl⟩
    have hF : Measurable F := hFdef ▸ hg.indicator hQm
    have hcv : ∫⁻ v, F (c + s • v) = ENNReal.ofReal |(s ^ n)⁻¹| * ∫⁻ z, F z := by
      have h1 : ∫⁻ w, F (c + w) ∂(Measure.map (fun v : Euclid n => s • v) volume)
          = ∫⁻ v, F (c + s • v) :=
        lintegral_map (hF.comp (measurable_const_add c)) (measurable_const_smul s)
      rw [← h1, Measure.map_addHaar_smul volume hs0.ne', lintegral_smul_measure,
        lintegral_add_left_eq_self F c, finrank_euclideanSpace_fin, smul_eq_mul]
    have hs2 : s⁻¹ ≤ 2 := by
      rw [inv_le_comm₀ hs0 two_pos]
      linarith
    calc ∫⁻ v in Q, g (c + s • v)
        = ∫⁻ v in Q, F (c + s • v) := by
          refine setLIntegral_congr_fun hQm fun v hv => ?_
          rw [hFdef, Set.indicator_of_mem (hcs v hv)]
      _ ≤ ∫⁻ v, F (c + s • v) := setLIntegral_le_lintegral _ _
      _ = ENNReal.ofReal |(s ^ n)⁻¹| * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z := by
          rw [hcv, hFdef, lintegral_indicator hQm]
      _ ≤ 2 ^ n * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z := by
          gcongr
          calc ENNReal.ofReal |(s ^ n)⁻¹| = ENNReal.ofReal s⁻¹ ^ n := by
                rw [abs_of_pos (by positivity), ← inv_pow, ENNReal.ofReal_pow (by positivity)]
            _ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal 2 ^ n := by gcongr
            _ = 2 ^ n := by rw [ENNReal.ofReal_ofNat]
  have hmeas : Measurable (fun p : Euclid n × Euclid n => g ((1 - t) • p.2 + t • p.1)) :=
    hg.comp (by fun_prop)
  rcases le_total (1 / 2 : ℝ) t with h | h
  · rw [lintegral_lintegral_swap (f := fun x y => g ((1 - t) • y + t • x)) hmeas.aemeasurable]
    calc ∫⁻ y in Q, ∫⁻ x in Q, g ((1 - t) • y + t • x)
        ≤ ∫⁻ _ in Q, 2 ^ n * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z := by
          refine setLIntegral_mono' hQm fun y hy => ?_
          refine key ((1 - t) • y) t h fun v hv => ?_
          exact hQc hy hv (by linarith) ht0 (by ring)
      _ = 2 ^ n * volume Q * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z := by
          rw [setLIntegral_const]
          ring
  · calc ∫⁻ x in Q, ∫⁻ y in Q, g ((1 - t) • y + t • x)
        ≤ ∫⁻ _ in Q, 2 ^ n * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z := by
          refine setLIntegral_mono' hQm fun x hx => ?_
          calc ∫⁻ y in Q, g ((1 - t) • y + t • x)
              = ∫⁻ y in Q, g (t • x + (1 - t) • y) :=
                lintegral_congr fun y => by rw [add_comm]
            _ ≤ 2 ^ n * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z := by
                refine key (t • x) (1 - t) (by linarith) fun v hv => ?_
                rw [add_comm]
                exact hQc hv hx (by linarith) ht0 (by ring)
      _ = 2 ^ n * volume Q * ∫⁻ z in Q, g z := by
          rw [setLIntegral_const]
          ring
proof_key_steps: One-variable bound: if s ≥ 1/2 and c + sQ ⊆ Q, then ∫⁻_Q g(c + sv) dv ≤ ∫⁻ (1_Q g)(c + sv) dv = s^{−n} ∫⁻_Q g ≤ 2ⁿ ∫⁻_Q g (Haar scaling, translation invariance).
(x, y) ↦ g((1 − t)y + tx) is measurable.
t ≥ 1/2: swap the order (Tonelli), then for each y ∈ Q apply the bound with c = (1 − t)y, s = t (convexity).
t ≤ 1/2: for each x ∈ Q apply the bound with c = tx, s = 1 − t (convexity).
Integrate the constant 2ⁿ ∫⁻_Q g over Q to get 2ⁿ Lⁿ(Q) ∫⁻_Q g.

audit.reason: The prose and type agree on measurable convex Q, measurable ENNReal-valued g and t∈[0,1]. Indicator extension, positive dilation and translation invariance establish the one-variable estimate. Tonelli and the correctly weighted variable choices cover both halves and endpoints. All operations remain valid for infinite lower integrals and zero measure; no finiteness assumption or circular dependency is hidden.
